FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Pirimiphos-methyl, technical is employed in the preparation of insecticidal formulations.

Pirimiphos-methyl is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) for the pesticidal chemical O-2-diethylamino-6-methylpyrimidin-4-yl-~~O-dimethylphosphorothioate. The empirical and structural formulae and molecular mass of pirimiphos-methyl are given below:

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value . in this standard.

The material shall be in the form a dark straw coloured to red/brown liquid at temperatures above 20�C. The material may contain crystals of pirimiphosmethyl in traces and shall be free from extraneous matter. 3.2 Miscibility
with Trimethyl Benzene, Technical

Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in IS 10946 : 1984.
NOTES 1 Before drawing representative samples, drums shall be checked for the presence of crystals and if found, must be thawed. To facilitate this, the drums may be stored in a warm room or partially immersed in moderately hot water ( maximum temperature 50�C ) for a period of not more than 24 hours prior to sampling. 2 Once received in the laboratory, the samples be stored at a temperature below 25�C. 7 TESTS shall

One part of the material shall be completely miscible with three parts of trimethyl benzene, technical, showing not more than a faint turbidity. 3.3 The material shall also comply requirements specified in Table 1. 4 PACKING The material shall be packed in clean and dry mild steel drums suitably lacquered from inside. DETERMINATION B-l GENERAL A portion of the sample is dissolved in a chloroform containing internal standard like. The active n-octadecane ingredient content is estimated gas chromatographically by comparing with a reference standard of known purity. B-2 APPARATUS B-2.1 Gas Chromatograph A gas chromatograph fitted with a flame ionization detector and an integrator-cum-recorder. The suggestive operating conditions are given below, which can be changed provided standardization is done: Column Glass, 2 m long and 6 mm 0.D packed with 1~ percent SE30 on acid washed celite 345 ( 100-120 mesh ). Condition the column by purging with nitrogen at 300�C overnight. After conditioning, pretreat the column with 3 injections each of 10 ~"1 of Silyl 8 at one minute intervals to avoid tailing of the peaks and to obtain better efficiency. OF PIRIMIPHOS-METHYL CONTENT to the mark with and then make up the volume chloroform.

B-4.2 Preparation of Standard Pirimiphos-Methyl Standard Solution Weigh accurately about 0'2 g of standard pirimiphos-methyl into a lOO-ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in IO ml of chloroform. Add 25 ml of internal standard solution from a burette, shake to dissolve the pirimiphos-methyl and make up the volume with chloroform. B-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution Weigh accurately a quantity of sample to contain 0'2 g of pirimiphos-methyl into a lOO-ml volumetric flask and add 10 ml chloroform. Add 25 ml of internal standard solution from a burette and shake to dissolve the pirimiphos-methyl sample and make up the volume with chloroform. B-4.4 Estimation Before starting the analysis, inject twice 3 rl of standard pirimiphos-methyl to equiliberate the system and use the data from these chromatograms to set the integrator parameters. Carry out the duplicate injections of standard and sample solutions and record the integrated areas for each peak. B-S CALCULATION Pirimiphos-methyl

Standard Mark I The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity Details of conditions under which a licence for the to that standard as a further safeguard. use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
